sentences.en: A Lion asleep in his lair was waked up by a Mouse running over his face.
sentences.zh: 一只狮子在洞穴里睡觉，被一只从脸上跑过的老鼠弄醒了。

sentences.en: Losing his temper he seized it with his paw and was about to kill it.
sentences.zh: 他动了怒，用爪子抓住它，正要弄死它。

sentences.en: The Mouse, terrified, piteously entreated him to spare its life.
sentences.zh: 老鼠吓得要命，可怜巴巴地哀求他饶自己一命。

sentences.en: "Please let me go," it cried, "and one day I will repay you for your kindness."
sentences.zh: 「请放我走吧，」它叫道，「总有一天我会报答您的恩情。」

sentences.en: The idea of so insignificant a creature ever being able to do anything for him amused the Lion so much that he laughed aloud …
sentences.zh: 想到这么一个微不足道的小东西居然能帮上自己的忙，狮子觉得十分可笑，竟笑出声来……

sentences.en: … and good-humouredly let it go.
sentences.zh: ……便好脾气地把它放了。

sentences.en: But the Mouse's chance came, after all.
sentences.zh: 可老鼠的机会终究还是来了。

sentences.en: One day the Lion got entangled in a net which had been spread for game by some hunters …
sentences.zh: 有一天，狮子被几个猎人张设捕猎的网缠住了……

sentences.en: … and the Mouse heard and recognised his roars of anger and ran to the spot.
sentences.zh: ……老鼠听见并认出了他愤怒的吼声，便跑到那里。

sentences.en: Without more ado it set to work to gnaw the ropes with its teeth, and succeeded before long in setting the Lion free.
sentences.zh: 它二话不说就用牙咬那些绳子，没多久便把狮子放开。

sentences.en: "There!" said the Mouse, "you laughed at me when I promised I would repay you: but now you see, even a Mouse can help a Lion."
sentences.zh: 「您看！」老鼠说，「我答应报答您的时候，您还笑我；可如今您看到了，就连一只老鼠也能帮上狮子的忙。」

sentences.en: A thirsty Crow found a Pitcher with some water in it …
sentences.zh: 一只口渴的乌鸦找到一只水罐，里面有些水……

sentences.en: … but so little was there that, try as she might, she could not reach it with her beak …
sentences.zh: ……可水太少，她怎么试，嘴也够不到……

sentences.en: … and it seemed as though she would die of thirst within sight of the remedy.
sentences.zh: ……眼看解渴的东西就在眼前，她却像是要渴死了。

sentences.en: At last she hit upon a clever plan.
sentences.zh: 最后她想到一个巧办法。

sentences.en: She began dropping pebbles into the Pitcher, and with each pebble the water rose a little higher until at last it reached the brim …
sentences.zh: 她开始往罐里丢小石子，每丢一颗，水就升高一点，直到最后升到罐口……

sentences.en: … and the knowing bird was enabled to quench her thirst.
sentences.zh: ……这只聪明的鸟便得以解了渴。

sentences.en: Necessity is the mother of invention.
sentences.zh: 需要是发明之母。

sentences.en: The Hares once gathered together and lamented the unhappiness of their lot, exposed as they were to dangers on all sides and lacking the …
sentences.zh: 野兔们曾聚在一起哀叹自己命苦：它们四面受敌，又缺少……

sentences.en: … strength and the courage to hold their own.
sentences.zh: ……保护自己的力气和勇气。

sentences.en: Men, dogs, birds and beasts of prey were all their enemies, and killed and devoured them daily …
sentences.zh: 人、狗、鸟和猛兽都是它们的敌人，天天捕杀吞食它们……

sentences.en: … and sooner than endure such persecution any longer, they one and all determined to end their miserable lives.
sentences.zh: ……它们再不愿忍受这样的迫害，便一致决定结束这悲惨的性命。

sentences.en: Thus resolved and desperate, they rushed in a body towards a neighbouring pool, intending to drown themselves.
sentences.zh: 既下了这样的决心，它们便绝望地成群奔向附近一个水塘，打算投水自尽。

sentences.en: On the bank were sitting a number of Frogs, who …
sentences.zh: 岸上坐着一群青蛙，它们……

sentences.en: … when they heard the noise of the Hares as they ran, with one accord leaped into the water and hid themselves in the depths.
sentences.zh: ……听见野兔奔跑的声响，便一齐跳进水里，躲到深处去了。

sentences.en: Then one of the older Hares who was wiser than the rest cried out to his companions, "Stop, my friends, take heart …
sentences.zh: 这时，一只比同伴们都聪明的年长野兔向大伙喊道：「停下吧，朋友们，振作起来……」

sentences.en: … don't let us destroy ourselves after all …
sentences.zh: 「……我们终究不必自寻短见……」

sentences.en: … see, here are creatures who are afraid of us, and who must, therefore, be still more timid than ourselves."
sentences.zh: 「……看，这里有怕我们的生灵，可见它们必定比我们更胆小。」
